RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the successful candidate are men, making it virtually impossible that sex discrimination played a role in choosing him over you. An all-male selection panel is common in structural engineering due to industry demographics and does not indicate bias against male applicants.

Raising the panel's gender composition would damage your credibility, as there is no basis for a sex discrimination claim when the successful applicant is of the same sex. 

The stated hiring rationale—emphasizing client relationships over technical tenure—suggests the decision was based on business development skills or organizational fit. Follow up politely for constructive feedback on your interview performance, but leave the panel's composition out of the discussion.
